messages:
Sarah (Sales): FYI prospect wants to run BYO-KMS "chaos" testing during the POC — kill/rotate keys and simulate HSM failover. They want a firm answer on whether we can support it and what the billing impact is. Need an ops runbook + cost scenarios by Friday.
Mike (CryptoOps): Can you share specifics? e.g., will they request automated rotation during the test or just simulated endpoint failures? Also what's the expected QPS and key usage pattern?
Sarah (Sales): They said: ~200 QPS p95, mostly short-lived signing calls, test window ~2 hours. Plan: trigger HSM node removal, force key rotation, and then validate application fallback. They're using a customer HSM (BYO) with CloudHSM-like behavior.
Anya (Solutions): We can do a staged dry-run in our staging env. Proposed steps:
1) Create a dedicated BYO key alias in staging.
2) Keep automatic rotation off, run manual rotation command: `redwood key rotate --alias prod-byo --force`.
3) Simulate node loss by blocking connections from a test agent to HSM subnet.
4) Verify fallback to Redwood-managed KEK and confirm audit logs.
We should document exact rollback commands and admin console steps.
Oliver (Pricing): For billing: HSM egress + dedicated ops time + possible elevated SLA for the window. Ballpark: HSM connector hours (~$120/hr) + 8 ops hours for prep/cutover. Need QPS and token size to estimate metered cost. Also, if they force re-encryption of object store during rotation, that could be significant.
Mike (CryptoOps): Important: during forced rotation we won't accept re-encryption jobs automatically unless they opt in. Recommend we provide a 'no-reencrypt' fallback to avoid prolonged egress. Also need customer-signed attestation before we run destructive tests.
Sarah (Sales): They asked about 'ephemeral rotation' — rotating every few minutes just for the test. Is that permitted?
Anya (Solutions): Not recommended in prod; for POC we can do limited ephemeral rotations in staging only. We'll need to disable caching and ensure KV cache invalidation logic is exercised — otherwise the app might just reuse stale tokens.
LegalBot: Heads-up: need a signed addendum for destructive testing and a short checklist: indemnity clause, data-handling boundaries, and retention policy for logs. See https://redwood.internal/legal/poi-test-addendum
deploy-bot: Scheduled: staging-dryrun-byok at 2026-03-24T10:00Z (created by Anya).
Oliver (Pricing): If we assume 200 QPS for 2 hours and 4k token avg size, estimate extra token cost ~$X and HSM connector cost as above. I'll formalize scenarios: (A) no re-encrypt (B) full re-encrypt. Need confirmation of object-store size and number of keys.
Mike (CryptoOps): Ops runbook items (short): firewall whitelist for test agent, pre-signed attestation, rollback console steps, who to call for emergency (oncall @crypto-sre), retention of audit logs (90d default), and a data-destruction confirmation.
Sarah (Sales): OK I'll collect object-store size and confirm that they sign the addendum. Can you draft the ops runbook checklist (Anya/Mike)? Oliver — plz send the two billing scenarios.
Anya (Solutions): I'll draft runbook checklist and include exact command snippets and the minimal set of monitoring checks. Will share a doc link by EOD.
Oliver (Pricing): Will do — I’ll post two line-item scenarios and a short SOW delta for destructive testing.
Sarah (Sales): Thanks team. Quick Q: is there any enterprise blocker (compliance/legal) that would flat-out stop this test?
LegalBot: If customer data or keys traverse non-approved regions or if the test requires access to customer plaintext outside agreed scopes, we block. Otherwise sign the addendum and we can greenlight with ops controls.
Mike (CryptoOps): One more: ensure they provide a test account with limited privileges. No production credentials.
Sarah (Sales): Great — will confirm and sync back. :thumbsup:
